human_owner.summary: Approved in advance by the owner through auto mode; the Claude reviewer decides.

non_blocking_findings.finding: Small synergist credit to the short head of biceps and coracobrachialis comes from the horizontal_adduction table weights. This is a tracer-table artifact, not a definition error.
The staggered, stepping stance is only partly captured by bilateral working-side leg actions. The frames do not resolve per-leg loading, so the assist-level credit is reasonable but approximate.
non_blocking_findings.suggested_correction: Optionally note in the assumptions that the leg drive is approximated as symmetric assist extension.

model_reviewer.summary: The definition fits the source. The instructions and frames show a three-point crouch with the ball in front, then a pull of the ball to the chest and an explosive two-handed forward release over two steps. A bilateral laterality and an open-chain label suit a released ball. Elbow extension and horizontal shoulder adduction as primary actions give a sensible chest-pass pattern: pectoralis major and triceps are the primary movers, with anterior deltoid and serratus anterior as synergists. Assist-weighted hip, knee and ankle extension credits the leg drive from the stance and steps without making the legs primary. Grip and wrist_stability fit the ball held in both hands before release. Postural_stabilization and scapular_anchoring give a plausible trunk and scapular base. The movement-family labels (jump_and_throw, horizontal_push) are reasonable. No biomechanically material claim is unsupported or contradicted.
